ai.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
ai.brief: OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet won’t share your actual credit card info with its AI agents. OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet won’t share your actual credit card info with its AI agents. After adding a card to the wallet, your Dots agents can use it to buy things in response to your prompts, but they’ll check in with you each time before checking out. OpenAI’s support page says every purchase with ChatGPT Wallet requires a security check with biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan. After you review the AI agent’s purchase and sign off on it, OpenAI says that, similar to using tap to pay , Apple Pay , or Google Wallet , it substitutes your credit card details with a payment token, so your actual card info isn’t shared with your Dots agent or the business you’re buying from. ”

sec.title: SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions
sec.brief: In this article ScreenConnect architecture and attack surfaces Attack chain overview Mitigation and protection guidance Indicators of compromise and supporting artifacts References Learn More Beginning on November 11, 2026, ConnectWise reported an active campaign of a threat actor gaining unauthorized access to cloud-hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect instances belonging to managed service providers (MSPs). Microsoft Threat Intelligence has confirmed ConnectWise’s reported activity and we have also observed threat actors abusing ScreenConnect, a legitimate remote-support application, to install unauthorized remote-access clients and deploy a malicious worm, SCKit, on ConnectWise customer managed endpoints. Additionally, Microsoft analyzed the malicious worm’s behavior: deployment starts with commands issued through ScreenConnect to silently install an identical client connected to threat actor-controlled infrastructure. A batch launcher retrieves a PowerShell decoder that decrypts and extracts SCKit using device-specific key material.
